course_map.title: A quadratic form as a directional cost
course_map.worked_example_capability: Evaluate and visualize a small positive form
course_map.assessment_target: Evaluate and visualize a small positive form

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: A positive quadratic form is q(v)=v^T G v with symmetric G; write its cross term and units. Use G=[[2,1],[1,2]] in inverse-length-squared units as an explicitly synthetic example. For displacement it yields dimensionless cost; for velocity it yields rate-squared cost. Positivity follows q= (vx+vy)^2+vx^2+vy^2.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For unit direction e1, q=2; for n=(1,1)/sqrt(2), q=3; for n=(1,-1)/sqrt(2),q=1. Thus the q=1 contour is an ellipse with principal semiaxes1 and1/sqrt(3) length units along the two diagonal directions. Plot these anchors when producing the lesson.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: v=(1,2) gives q=2+4+8=14 in the corresponding units; v=(1,-1) gives2. Reversing v preserves q, while the underlying signed vector is retained. A matrix diag(1,-1) is not positive because q(0,1)=-1.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A positive form is not a force law or automatically energy. Do not omit the2 G12 vx vy term. Source G_phase and the geometric Gram metric have different definitions even if both are symmetric.

course_map.title: From plane counts to phase cost
course_map.worked_example_capability: Derive the cost under the source ruler and time conventions
course_map.assessment_target: Derive the cost under the source ruler and time conventions

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Start from dimensionless plane counts q_j=n_j dot(x-o)/d_j with fixed normals, spacings and origin. If a phase-coordinate metric H is declared, rate cost qdot^T H qdot has units1/time^2 for dimensionless H. Derive a physical-coordinate pullback from the exact ruler map, not from unexplained symbol reuse.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic rulers n1=e1,d1=1L,n2=e2,d2=2L, H=I. Then qdot=(vx,vy/2) in1/T and rate cost=vx^2+vy^2/4 with the implied inverse-length factors. For v=(1,2)L/T this is2/T^2; integrating for3T gives6/T.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For v=(-1,2)L/T, qdot=(-1,1)/T and rate cost2/T^2, same as the prior example while count direction differs. Two1T segments give cumulative costs2/T and4/T. Keep signed phase counts alongside their positive cost.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A cost integrated over time is not the square of net count: opposite rates can sum to zero net count and still accumulate positive cost. Source ruler/time normalizations must be supplied before claiming the source value.

course_map.title: Pullbacks and coordinate changes
course_map.worked_example_capability: Verify a small matrix congruence without claiming new dynamics
course_map.assessment_target: Verify a small matrix congruence without claiming new dynamics

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Teach the full congruence W_qpc=B^T G_phase B/4 from x=B u/2. B maps dimensionless coordinates to length; G_phase has inverse-length-squared units under this classroom typing; W is dimensionless. For coordinate velocities, u_dot^T W u_dot has units1/time^2. Preserve matrix order, basis and precision.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic B=diag(2,1)L and G=[[2,1],[1,2]]L^-2 give W=[[2,1/2],[1/2,1/2]]. With u_dot=(1,2)/T, v=B u_dot/2=(1,1)L/T and both forms equal6/T^2. Calculate all off-diagonal entries, not just the diagonal.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: With u_dot=(2,-2)/T, v=(2,-1)L/T; both costs equal6/T^2. Recover u_dot=2 B^-1 v. Omitting the factor1/4 would multiply both intended pullback costs by4.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: The spectral JSON supplies a decimal G_phase for that analysis; it is not automatically the full locked G_phase,C,W_qpc and route certificate requested by SA27. The symbols, coordinate conventions and precision must be linked by source before substitution. No missing source C or W is invented.

course_map.title: Integrating cost along a path
course_map.worked_example_capability: Compute a discrete cumulative path cost with units
course_map.assessment_target: Compute a discrete cumulative path cost with units

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: For a piecewise-constant velocity path, cost J=sum dt_i v_i^T G v_i. Specify each positive duration, total time, endpoints, metric units and admissible interpolation. Retain the segment ledger and cumulative values, not just the total.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic G=[[2,1],[1,2]]L^-2, start(0,0)L, two1T segments. Straight velocities(1,0),(1,0)L/T have costs2/T and2/T, cumulative(2,4)/T and endpoint(2,0)L. Dogleg velocities(1,1),(1,-1) have segment costs6/T and2/T, cumulative(6,8)/T and the same endpoint.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Reverse the dogleg segment order: velocities(1,-1),(1,1), cumulative(2,8)/T, same total8/T and endpoint. Subdividing each straight1T segment into two half-T segments leaves total4/T; keep the new sampling map and original durations.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Summing costs without durations changes units and sampling dependence. Same endpoints alone do not ensure a fair comparison if total time, metric or obstacles differ. Retain quadrature/interpolation error for a nonconstant sampled path.

course_map.title: Route comparison and constraints
course_map.worked_example_capability: Compare admissible paths under one fixed specification
course_map.assessment_target: Compare admissible paths under one fixed specification

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Prove a synthetic minimum under fixed start/end, fixed T>0, constant positive G and unrestricted absolutely continuous paths with square-integrable velocity. Write v=vbar+delta, vbar=displacement/T and integral delta=0. Then J=T vbar^T G vbar+integral delta^T G delta. This supplies a lower bound reached by constant velocity if that path is admissible.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For displacement(2,0)L,T=2T_units and the same G, vbar=(1,0)L/T and lower bound4/T. Straight path attains4/T; dogleg has8/T. For two equal-duration segments vbar+delta and vbar-delta, excess=2 delta^T G delta>=0. Thus this declared problem has lower=upper=4/T,gap0.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For delta=(0,1)L/T, excess4/T reproduces the dogleg. If duration is changed to4T with the same displacement, straight speed halves and cost becomes2/T; it is a different optimization problem. If an obstacle excludes the straight path,4/T remains a lower bound but attainment is not established.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Comparing only two routes does not prove a global minimum; the decomposition proves it under the stated class. Do not substitute a different historical maximum-residual objective or these toy bounds for the named source least-cost certificate.

T20 merely names certificate fields and supplies no numeric path/bounds/gap. The parent retrieval status and this audit search both leave the full named source certificate unavailable. S03 records4.58938078934712923077736690075e-12, which is not literal zero.

course_map.title: Phase cost and physical coupling
course_map.worked_example_capability: Identify the additional observations needed to connect modeled cost to measured response
course_map.assessment_target: Identify the additional observations needed to connect modeled cost to measured response

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: A coordinate cost predicts a modeled quantity under its definitions. Connecting it to detector response requires an explicit transfer/coupling model, calibration, timing, orientation, exposure, source state and retained response residual. Teach nonidentifiability with a scalar product before proposing a discriminating observation.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic response y=k*r with known cost label q does not identify k and r if only y=6 is supplied: pairs(2,3) and(1,6) both fit. A source-reported input-equivalent energy is likewise distinct from transferred energy. Keep both candidate factorizations and the missing calibration.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: If an independently specified calibration provides r=3 in the appropriate units, the model gives k=2. For a second synthetic measurement y=7 with the same fixed r, predicted6 leaves residual1 in detector units. Retain it and state whether the coupling or additional state is being tested; do not refit every row silently.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A route minimizer, phase response and positive scalar cost do not identify force, extraction or an apparatus transfer law. The capstone must separately report its synthetic route proof and the exact missing-source retrieval checklist.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: A positive quadratic form is q(v)=v^T G v with symmetric G; write its cross term and units. Use G=[[2,1],[1,2]] in inverse-length-squared units as an explicitly synthetic example. For displacement it yields dimensionless cost; for velocity it yields rate-squared cost. Positivity follows q= (vx+vy)^2+vx^2+vy^2.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For unit direction e1, q=2; for n=(1,1)/sqrt(2), q=3; for n=(1,-1)/sqrt(2),q=1. Thus the q=1 contour is an ellipse with principal semiaxes1 and1/sqrt(3) length units along the two diagonal directions. Plot these anchors when producing the lesson.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: v=(1,2) gives q=2+4+8=14 in the corresponding units; v=(1,-1) gives2. Reversing v preserves q, while the underlying signed vector is retained. A matrix diag(1,-1) is not positive because q(0,1)=-1.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A positive form is not a force law or automatically energy. Do not omit the2 G12 vx vy term. Source G_phase and the geometric Gram metric have different definitions even if both are symmetric.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Start from dimensionless plane counts q_j=n_j dot(x-o)/d_j with fixed normals, spacings and origin. If a phase-coordinate metric H is declared, rate cost qdot^T H qdot has units1/time^2 for dimensionless H. Derive a physical-coordinate pullback from the exact ruler map, not from unexplained symbol reuse.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic rulers n1=e1,d1=1L,n2=e2,d2=2L, H=I. Then qdot=(vx,vy/2) in1/T and rate cost=vx^2+vy^2/4 with the implied inverse-length factors. For v=(1,2)L/T this is2/T^2; integrating for3T gives6/T.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For v=(-1,2)L/T, qdot=(-1,1)/T and rate cost2/T^2, same as the prior example while count direction differs. Two1T segments give cumulative costs2/T and4/T. Keep signed phase counts alongside their positive cost.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A cost integrated over time is not the square of net count: opposite rates can sum to zero net count and still accumulate positive cost. Source ruler/time normalizations must be supplied before claiming the source value.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Teach the full congruence W_qpc=B^T G_phase B/4 from x=B u/2. B maps dimensionless coordinates to length; G_phase has inverse-length-squared units under this classroom typing; W is dimensionless. For coordinate velocities, u_dot^T W u_dot has units1/time^2. Preserve matrix order, basis and precision.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic B=diag(2,1)L and G=[[2,1],[1,2]]L^-2 give W=[[2,1/2],[1/2,1/2]]. With u_dot=(1,2)/T, v=B u_dot/2=(1,1)L/T and both forms equal6/T^2. Calculate all off-diagonal entries, not just the diagonal.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: With u_dot=(2,-2)/T, v=(2,-1)L/T; both costs equal6/T^2. Recover u_dot=2 B^-1 v. Omitting the factor1/4 would multiply both intended pullback costs by4.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: The spectral JSON supplies a decimal G_phase for that analysis; it is not automatically the full locked G_phase,C,W_qpc and route certificate requested by SA27. The symbols, coordinate conventions and precision must be linked by source before substitution. No missing source C or W is invented.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: For a piecewise-constant velocity path, cost J=sum dt_i v_i^T G v_i. Specify each positive duration, total time, endpoints, metric units and admissible interpolation. Retain the segment ledger and cumulative values, not just the total.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic G=[[2,1],[1,2]]L^-2, start(0,0)L, two1T segments. Straight velocities(1,0),(1,0)L/T have costs2/T and2/T, cumulative(2,4)/T and endpoint(2,0)L. Dogleg velocities(1,1),(1,-1) have segment costs6/T and2/T, cumulative(6,8)/T and the same endpoint.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Reverse the dogleg segment order: velocities(1,-1),(1,1), cumulative(2,8)/T, same total8/T and endpoint. Subdividing each straight1T segment into two half-T segments leaves total4/T; keep the new sampling map and original durations.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Summing costs without durations changes units and sampling dependence. Same endpoints alone do not ensure a fair comparison if total time, metric or obstacles differ. Retain quadrature/interpolation error for a nonconstant sampled path.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Prove a synthetic minimum under fixed start/end, fixed T>0, constant positive G and unrestricted absolutely continuous paths with square-integrable velocity. Write v=vbar+delta, vbar=displacement/T and integral delta=0. Then J=T vbar^T G vbar+integral delta^T G delta. This supplies a lower bound reached by constant velocity if that path is admissible.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For displacement(2,0)L,T=2T_units and the same G, vbar=(1,0)L/T and lower bound4/T. Straight path attains4/T; dogleg has8/T. For two equal-duration segments vbar+delta and vbar-delta, excess=2 delta^T G delta>=0. Thus this declared problem has lower=upper=4/T,gap0.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For delta=(0,1)L/T, excess4/T reproduces the dogleg. If duration is changed to4T with the same displacement, straight speed halves and cost becomes2/T; it is a different optimization problem. If an obstacle excludes the straight path,4/T remains a lower bound but attainment is not established.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Comparing only two routes does not prove a global minimum; the decomposition proves it under the stated class. Do not substitute a different historical maximum-residual objective or these toy bounds for the named source least-cost certificate.

T20 merely names certificate fields and supplies no numeric path/bounds/gap. The parent retrieval status and this audit search both leave the full named source certificate unavailable. S03 records4.58938078934712923077736690075e-12, which is not literal zero.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Synthetic rounding example: exact1/3 versus decimal0.3333 leaves difference1/30000. Declaring truncation to four decimal places gives interval[0.3333,0.3334), which contains1/3. This is a supplied toy precision rule, not a rule inferred for the source closure. A candidate interval lower3.9,upper4.1 has gap0.2 in common cost units, not gap0.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: A coordinate cost predicts a modeled quantity under its definitions. Connecting it to detector response requires an explicit transfer/coupling model, calibration, timing, orientation, exposure, source state and retained response residual. Teach nonidentifiability with a scalar product before proposing a discriminating observation.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic response y=k*r with known cost label q does not identify k and r if only y=6 is supplied: pairs(2,3) and(1,6) both fit. A source-reported input-equivalent energy is likewise distinct from transferred energy. Keep both candidate factorizations and the missing calibration.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: If an independently specified calibration provides r=3 in the appropriate units, the model gives k=2. For a second synthetic measurement y=7 with the same fixed r, predicted6 leaves residual1 in detector units. Retain it and state whether the coupling or additional state is being tested; do not refit every row silently.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A route minimizer, phase response and positive scalar cost do not identify force, extraction or an apparatus transfer law. The capstone must separately report its synthetic route proof and the exact missing-source retrieval checklist.
